$comment: Pins the values a wrong TYPE or a wrong ENUM would silently mis-render. Enums: a wrong clusterProfile renders the dev topology and the drift hook cannot catch it. Booleans: Helm's `not`/`and`/`or`/`ternary` are strict — a knob set to 0 or "true" aborts the render with 'wrong type for value; expected bool; got int64', so the type is checked up front instead. Everything else stays permissive (no additionalProperties:false anywhere) — Helm injects `global`, and future tiers add keys. Every boolean leaf of values.yaml is typed here; scripts/values-schema-bools-check.py fails the build when a new one is added without a matching constraint.

instances.description: Instance count for this data tier. null (the default) = the cluster profile's count (clusterProfileInstances); an explicit integer wins over the profile.
Instance count for this data tier. null (the default) = the cluster profile's count (clusterProfileInstances); an explicit integer wins over the profile.

replicas.description: Pod count for this service. null (the default) = the cluster profile's count (clusterProfileReplicas), or 1 when the profile has no entry; an explicit integer — including 0, the scale-off — wins over the profile.

port.description: The port the container listens on and every piece of plumbing (Service targetPort, NetworkPolicy, probes) dials. The chart also sets the process's own port (PORT, or --port for redis), so an override moves the LISTENER too. ClamAV is the exception the render enforces: clamd takes its port from clamd.conf, so only 3310 is accepted.

clusterProfileInstances.description: clusterProfile-driven instance counts for the data tier (Keycloak, Postgres). An explicit data.<tier>.instances wins over these.

clusterProfileReplicas.description: clusterProfile-driven replica overrides. The order is the EXPLICIT value, then the profile, then 1: `services.<svc>.replicas` wins over this map when it is set (null by default = the profile applies).

global.$comment: Only the keys the chart interpolates into a shell are typed here — a shape the render would otherwise accept and the pod would execute. toolingArch lands in the kubectl URL path; kubeletToolsMirror is interpolated into the tools-init container's shell inside double quotes.

toolingArch.description: Forces the kubectl binary architecture the tools-init container downloads; empty = detect from uname -m. Constrained to the values the download URL accepts — the value is interpolated into the init container's shell, so anything outside the enum is rejected at render, not executed.

kubeletToolsMirror.description: Internal mirror for the kubectl download: [http[s]://]host[:port 1-65535][/multi/segment/prefix] — the scheme is optional and case-insensitive (scheme-less makes curl use plain HTTP), /release/... is appended, and the prefix may carry multiple path segments (the Nexus/Artifactory repository topology). No trailing slash (it would double the appended path's leading slash on strict routers). The host admits a colon only before a numeric port in the 1-65535 range, and the scheme only http(s): the value is interpolated into the tools-init container's shell inside double quotes, and any other shape (file://, https:mirror, :99999, shell metacharacters) is rejected at render.
